newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr edges higher as RBA stays silent.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr edges higher as RBA stays silent.

text.p: The Australian dollar edged higher in calm trade after the Reserve Bank stayed silent at its money market operation, the usual time for any policy announcement.

There has been much speculation the RBA would ease policy for a fifth time this cycle following its monthly board meeting on Tuesday, although in recent days a consensus had grown the bank would wait for further data before deciding.

There was still a risk the bank could cut Thursday morning should retail trade data today prove weak and the Federal Reserve leave U.S. rates steady at its policy meeting tonight, so dealers doubted the A$ could rally past US$0.7540 resistance.
By 9.45 am (2345 GMT) the local dollar had inched to US$0.7515/20 from an early US$0.7510/15 and was still short of Tuesday's late US$0.7525/30.

The modest reaction reflected the fact the market had largely priced in a "no change" outcome on Monday when a short covering rally lifted the currency from a 17-month low of US$0.7440 to a peak of US$0.7570 in one go.

Dealers said there could be scope for more should the RBA keep its silence on Thursday morning, since the market would assume it was on hold for a while, possibly until inflation and wages data were released on July 23/24.
The chance of a move Thursday should be easier to assess once today's retail trade and building approvals data are released.

It was a shock 1.7 percent dive in sales for April which first started analysts thinking about a fifth cut in RBA rates, and any further weakness this time would have the money market baying for an immediate easing.

Median forecasts do favour a rise of around 2.0 percent in May but estimates range from a 3.0 percent gain to a 0.3 percnet drop. Anything less than a 1.0 percent rise would be considered soft and an actual fall would see the dollar down sharply.
Building approvals are expected to rise around 2.0 percent after a 3.6 percent gain in April, which would provide further confirmation of of an on-going housing recovery.

Estimates range from a 3.0 percent drop to a 10.0 percent rise, with the loftier predictions based on expectations the approvals for a huge housing development at the Olympic village would be included in the May figures.

Analysts felt that if all the data were in line with forecasts, the chances were the RBA had decided to wait for the inflation and wages data and possibly until its next board meeting on August 5. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
